samples.summary: New `readRoot()` seam has no test that would fail if it were reverted to `this.doc.getRoot()`
samples.evidence: The two new mid-batch read tests ('a read inside a batch observes the batch's own earlier writes', 'a mid-batch read forced past the cache still sees the in-progress writes') assert that a read taken inside an open batch sees the batch's writes. But the code's own comment at yorkie-doc-store.ts readRoot() states that `getRoot()` "builds that proxy over the same clone root, so in practice it observes the in-progress writes" — i.e. these assertions hold both with and without the change under review. So the delta's central production change (routing reads through `activeRoot`) is exercised but not pinned: reverting `readRoot()` to `this.doc.getRoot()` would keep the suite green. A distinguishing test (e.g. asserting the read is taken from the ambient root, or a case where the getRoot proxy differs) is missing.
searchedFor: read new batch-read tests in yorkie-doc-store.test.ts

samples.summary: 'runs the body through the store batch' does not assert the store batch was used
samples.evidence: The test calls `doc.batch(() => doc.insertText(...))` and only asserts the text landed. With `MemDocStore`, `batch()` merely runs `fn` and pushes an undo checkpoint, so the assertion passes identically if `Doc.batch` were implemented as `fn()` with no `store.batch` call at all — the very thing the test name claims to verify. Nothing checks the one-undo-unit property (e.g. `canUndo`/undo-stack depth, or a spy on `store.batch`), so the batching contract of the new `Doc.batch` wrapper is uncovered on the happy path.

finding.summary: Nested-batch test asserts only the undo-unit count; it never checks the nested body's write was applied
finding.evidence: `it('a nested batch does not open a second undo unit')` performs `store.applyStyle(..., { italic: true })` inside an inner `store.batch(...)` and then asserts only `doc.getUndoStackForTest().length === before + 1`. If the nested fast path (`if (this.activeRoot) { fn(); return; }` plus `withUpdate` reusing `activeRoot`) dropped or misrouted the inner write entirely, the undo-stack count would be unchanged and the test would still pass. No assertion on `italic` after the batch, and none through a fresh store. The MemDocStore nested test (packages/docs/test/store/memory.test.ts) has the same shape: it only asserts the post-undo text, never that the nested `'?'` insert landed first.

verdict.reason: The finding claims the nested-batch test in yorkie-doc-store.test.ts asserts only the undo-unit count, with "No assertion on `italic` after the batch, and none through a fresh store." Reading the test refutes this directly. yorkie-doc-store.test.ts:712-734 asserts `doc.getUndoStackForTest().length === before + 1` AND THEN, at lines 725-733, carries a comment naming precisely the drop/misroute hazard the reviewer describes, followed by `const fromTree = new YorkieDocStore(doc).getBlock(block.id)!;` with `expect(fromTree.inlines[0].style.italic).toBe(true)` — an assertion on the nested body's write, taken through a fresh store. The freshness is real: `cachedDoc`/`dirty` are per-instance private fields initialized to null/true (yorkie-doc-store.ts:557-558) and `readRoot()` falls back to `this.doc.getRoot()` with no activeRoot (line 625), so the new instance reads the CRDT rather than the mutating store's optimistic cache. If the nested fast path dropped the inner applyStyle, italic would be undefined and the test would fail. The secondary MemDocStore claim (memory.test.ts:255-269) is factually accurate — it asserts only post-undo text and canUndo — but is not blocking: the nested path in memory.ts:176-188 only increments batchDepth and calls fn() directly, with no alternate write context to misroute into, and insertText writes unconditionally; batched writes landing is already pinned at memory.test.ts:290-293 and 305-310. That residue is minor at most, and the finding's headline location and quoted evidence are false.
